column1: # Disagreements with the HTTP/2 references that are understood, and why.
# Five tab-separated fields: a case tag (a glob, `|` separating alternatives),
# a reference (a glob, `|` too), the kind of difference (a glob over
# `conn:<CODE>`; `conn:CLOSED` is a connection the reference hung up on without
# a GOAWAY; a reset the reference made by answering 4xx is `HTTP<status>`), a
# class (diff_h2.py CLASSES) and a sentence. The first match wins. A
# disagreement that matches no rule fails the run, and so does a rule that
# matches nothing. A rule for a generated case (`gen:`, `genhd:`) speaks for a
# family of single mutations, each of which makes a valid stream invalid in
# one way; the families were checked by reading the cases behind each rule.
# Read with documentation/rfc9113.md, which states what this library enforces.

column5: section 3.4 lets a GOAWAY be omitted for an invalid preface, and the reference closes without one; this library sends GOAWAY(PROTOCOL_ERROR)
section 3.4: the first frame after the preface MUST be SETTINGS (not an ACK, not another type); the reference does not insist

column1: # ---- limits: this library's defaults against each reference's own ---------------------------

column5: a limit of this library's default GHTTP_H2Limits (100 fields counting the pseudo-header fields, 16 CONTINUATION frames, 16 KiB a field, 64 KiB of header list) ends the connection with ENHANCE_YOUR_CALM; the reference has another limit, or none, and the codes differ
section 5.1.2: a stream beyond the advertised limit MUST be a stream error (PROTOCOL_ERROR or REFUSED_STREAM); h2 ends the connection, this library refuses the stream (REFUSED_STREAM)
section 4.2: a frame too small for its mandatory fields is FRAME_SIZE_ERROR; nghttp2 says PROTOCOL_ERROR and Go closes without a GOAWAY (an error from its frame reader that is not a connection error)
section 6.5: an ACK with a payload is FRAME_SIZE_ERROR; h2 raises PROTOCOL_ERROR
section 6.2: padding longer than the payload is a connection error PROTOCOL_ERROR; Go resets the stream
a zero WINDOW_UPDATE is a stream error (6.9) but the stream is idle, which is a connection error (5.1): the RFC does not order them; Go takes the first
section 6.3: a PRIORITY frame of the wrong length MUST be a STREAM error FRAME_SIZE_ERROR; the reference ends the connection
RFC 7540 section 5.3.1 made a stream depending on itself an error; RFC 9113 deprecated the priority scheme and dropped the rule, so this library reads the fields and ignores them
section 6.5.3 does not make a SETTINGS ACK that acknowledges nothing an error; this library ignores it
section 4.1 and 6.8: the reserved bit in a GOAWAY's last stream id MUST be ignored on receipt
section 6.9: the reserved bit of a WINDOW_UPDATE increment MUST be ignored on receipt
Go ends the connection (PROTOCOL_ERROR) on a SETTINGS identifier that repeats; sections 6.5.2 and 6.5.3 only say the values are applied in order, and this library does

after the peer's GOAWAY h2 treats a HEADERS frame as invalid input (its state machine is CLOSED) and Go starts a graceful shutdown that accepts no new stream; section 6.8 describes what the sender of a GOAWAY may do, not what its receiver must refuse, and this library serves what arrives
nghttp2 hands the application the octets of a DATA frame as they arrive; this library delivers a frame whole, so a stream that ends inside one delivers none of it
section 5.1.1: a stream identifier that is not higher than every one already used MUST be a connection error PROTOCOL_ERROR; nghttp2 ignores the HEADERS frame

section 5.1: a frame on a closed stream MAY be a connection error STREAM_CLOSED, which this library chooses; the reference makes it a stream error, or ignores it, or ends the connection with another code
section 5.1: a frame on a half-closed (remote) stream MUST be a STREAM error STREAM_CLOSED; nghttp2 ends the connection
the stream errors sections 6.9 and 8.1.1 require (a zero WINDOW_UPDATE on a stream; a malformed message): the reference ends the connection instead

a sender that does not wait for WINDOW_UPDATE is within its window only if the receiver has credited it back; this library credits at once, h2 and Go as the application reads, so a body sent back to back is an error there and not here (section 6.9.1 leaves the policy to the receiver)

column1: # ---- RFC 9113 8.2.1 and 8.3: names, values and control data that are wrong, per reference ----------
# The tags below are the cases in which one side delivered the request and the
# other refused it, or refused it differently. In the notes, MUST and SHOULD are
# RFC 9113's own: section 8.2.1 MUSTs refuse a field name with 0x00-0x20, A-Z,
# 0x7f-0xff or (outside a pseudo-header) a colon, and a value with NUL, LF, CR or
# whitespace at either end, and SHOULDs validate the rest against RFC 9110's
# definitions, which is what this library does (documentation/rfc9113.md).
# nghttp2 drops a field it finds invalid and delivers the rest of the request

column5: section 8.2.1 says a request with such a name or value MUST be treated as malformed; nghttp2 reports the field to on_invalid_header_callback, drops it and delivers the request (checked: the delivered request lacks the field)
section 8.2.1 SHOULD validate a field name against RFC 9110's token, which these characters are not in; this library does, the reference checks only the MUST list
nghttp2 drops a content-length it finds invalid (not digits, or with whitespace) and delivers the request; this library refuses a request whose content-length is not a list of one value in digits
RFC 9110 section 8.6 allows a content-length repeated with identical values (and a list of them); the reference refuses it
section 8.2.1's MUST list does not include DEL or other control characters in a value; the reference drops or refuses the field

section 8.3.1 allows a request with no :authority and no Host (no authority to convey), an OPTIONS request with :path "*", and does not forbid a repeated Host; nghttp2 refuses them (and a scheme or authority with a slash, which this library does not check)

section 8.3.1 describes the values of the request pseudo-header fields (a method token, an absolute-path, an authority without userinfo, a scheme) and 8.2.1 SHOULD validate against RFC 9110: this library refuses a value outside those grammars, the reference accepts it

section 8.1.1: a message whose content-length differs from the DATA is malformed, including one that ends at its HEADERS with a non-zero length; this library refuses it there, the reference delivers the request

a trailer section with a content-length (RFC 9110 section 6.5.1: framing fields MUST NOT be in a trailer) or one that ends the stream short of the announced length (8.1.1: malformed) is accepted by h2; this library resets the stream
section 8.5: on a connected stream only DATA and stream management frames are allowed and anything else MUST be a stream error; the reference reads a second HEADERS as trailers

this library adds a Host field from :authority and joins split Cookie fields (section 8.2.3), as its Request type is the HTTP/1.1 one; the probe cannot tell its Host from an identical one the peer sent, and the reference passes the fields as they came

RFC 9110 section 7.2 and RFC 9113 section 8.3.1: a Host field beside :authority must say the same, and a request in which it does not is one a recipient may refuse; this library makes it malformed (a stream error), the references deliver it with one of the two

section 8.3.1: a server SHOULD treat a request whose Host differs from :authority as malformed (after normalisation); this library does not compare them (documentation/rfc9113.md); h2 refuses a byte-wise difference
section 8.3.1 allows a request with no authority to convey, and OPTIONS with :path "*"; h2 requires :authority or Host, and a path that starts with a slash
a content-length above 2^64 is not a length any body can have: h2 ends the connection, this library resets the stream, and the DATA the request goes on to carry differs
section 8.5: a connected stream carries opaque data and is not message-framed; h2 applies the content-length to it
section 8.1.1: a malformed message MUST be a stream error (here PROTOCOL_ERROR); h2 ends the connection with a GOAWAY instead
section 8.1.1: a malformed request MUST be treated as a stream error and a server MAY send a response before resetting; Go answers 400 and does not reset

Go reads a content-length it cannot parse as unknown and accepts the request (an invalid or conflicting content-length is malformed, section 8.1.1 and RFC 9110 8.6); a body that does not match then fails at the read
section 8.2.1: a value that starts or ends with whitespace MUST be treated as malformed; Go delivers it with the whitespace
a te field other than "trailers" (8.2.2), a :path that is not an absolute path or "*" for OPTIONS, and a method that is not a token are malformed (8.3.1); Go delivers the request
section 8.2.1 SHOULD validate fields against RFC 9110: a path with a space or a non-ASCII octet, an empty authority and one with a space are refused here and delivered by Go

a te of "Trailers" (the RFC's token comparison is case-insensitive), a path with a bad percent-encoding, and a scheme that is not lower-case http or https are accepted by this library, and not by Go, which parses the request URL and answers 400
Go handles the Trailer and Expect request fields itself (announces trailers, answers 100-continue) and lists them differently
Go keeps a request's trailers only for the names its Trailer field announced; the others are discarded before the handler runs
a trailer section with a framing or connection-specific field: both reset the stream, Go after having reported the request ended
a body that does not match its content-length: both reset the stream with PROTOCOL_ERROR; Go may have reported part of the body first and resets with the error of its own reader
Go reports the first Host as the request's authority when no :authority came; this library reports what the peer put in :authority
a list or an extra field of content-length values: Go treats it as unknown, and a CONNECT stream with a content-length is checked as a message by Go and not by this library
section 8.5: on a connected stream only DATA and stream management frames are allowed and anything else MUST be a stream error; Go reads a second HEADERS as trailers

column1: # ---- how the reference reads the same bytes cut differently ----------------------------------------

column5: nghttp2 counts the pieces a header block arrives in as CONTINUATION frames against its limit (CVE-2024-28182 hardening), so a header block of two or more frames fed a byte at a time ends the connection with no GOAWAY and fed whole does not
h2 reads the frames of one chunk against the state the whole chunk leaves, so a request after a GOAWAY is an error in one split and not in the other
section 4.2: a dynamic table size update is only valid at the start of a header block (COMPRESSION_ERROR otherwise); Go's decoder applies it wherever it comes
nghttp2's decoder refuses a name plus value above 65536 octets (NGHTTP2_HD_MAX_NV); this library's limit is the one it was given
nghttp2 requires a block to open with a dynamic table size update after the decoder's maximum was set below 4096 (section 4.2); this decoder, handed a table already of that size, does not

column1: # ---- generated mutations: families, by what each side did -------------------------------------------
# Each case is a valid stream with ONE change (diff_h2.py corpus: an octet, a
# frame's length, type, flags or stream, a frame cut, repeated, dropped, swapped
# or split). Reading the cases behind each rule, the families are these; "ours"
# the reference's own process crashed (Go, x/net v0.50.0)

column5: golang.org/x/net v0.50.0 indexes its table of frame parsers by frame type with holes at 0x0a to 0x0f (the table is sized for PRIORITY_UPDATE, 0x10), so the server calls a nil function on a client's frame of one of those types, such as ALTSVC (0x0a) and ORIGIN (0x0c), and the whole process dies: a one-frame denial of service. This library treats an unknown type as an extension and ignores it (section 5.5)

column1: # the stream ends inside a frame (finish() on this library says so)

column5: this library does not act on a frame until it is whole; nghttp2 decodes the field block and DATA as the octets arrive, so it has refused a field, reset a stream or delivered part of a body that this library has not reached when the input ends
this library does not act on a frame until it is whole; the reference has acted on a part of the stream's last frame that this library holds back

column1: # both end the connection: the code, or what had been delivered, differs

column5: both end the connection at a bad frame, with different codes (a malformed frame header is FRAME_SIZE_ERROR or PROTOCOL_ERROR depending on which check runs first; a bad preface is answered with a GOAWAY here and closed silently by the reference, section 3.4) or after having delivered different requests before it

column1: # this library ended the connection and the reference went on

column5: a frame for a stream whose number is lower than one already opened (closed implicitly, section 5.1.1) or on a stream that has ended: this library ends the connection (section 5.1 lets it: a MAY), the reference ignores the frame or answers with a stream error
section 3.4: the first frame after the preface MUST be SETTINGS, and RST_STREAM on an idle stream is a connection error (5.1); the reference accepts the stream without them, or with them

a frame header that is refused as soon as it is read (a length over the limit or wrong for its type, a first frame that is not SETTINGS, a type that makes the length wrong) when the input ends before the frame's payload does: the reference waits for the payload, and gives its answer only if the stream goes on

column1: # the reference ended the connection and this library did not

column5: a stream error (a malformed message, a frame on a half-closed stream, PRIORITY of the wrong size, a body that does not match its content-length), or a SETTINGS ACK nobody asked for, or a GOAWAY from a client, answered by the reference with a connection error where this library resets the stream or goes on (sections 5.1, 6.3, 6.5.3, 8.1.1)

column1: # both went on, and what they delivered differs

column5: both reset the stream (or both end the input) but nghttp2 delivers the octets of a DATA frame that came before the mismatch and this library delivers a frame only whole
both reset the stream, but nghttp2 delivers the octets of a DATA frame that came before the mismatch and this library delivers a frame only whole

[flaky] a HEADERS block that the RFC makes a stream error (a second block that is not trailers, then a third; a block after END_STREAM): Go resets the stream, answers 400, or ends the connection with PROTOCOL_ERROR according to when its handler goroutine runs. Only the reference side is flaky: this library's own answer (ok, with a stream reset) is the left of the kind and is pinned by H2Streams.AHeadersBlockOnAHalfClosedStreamWithoutEndStreamIsAStreamError and H2Streams.AThirdHeadersBlockIsDiscardedAfterTheMalformedSecond

nghttp2 drops a field it finds invalid (a name or value outside section 8.2.1's lists, an invalid content-length) and delivers the request, or accepts a header block this library resets the stream for

a header block this library resets the stream for (a field value, name or pseudo-header the sections 8.2 and 8.3 forbid, a content-length that is invalid, trailers that do not end the stream) is accepted by h2

Go accepts what this library resets the stream for: whitespace around a value, an invalid content-length, a pseudo-header or path that is not valid (section 8.2.1 and 8.3.1), or a frame after which this library has stopped
Go keeps a request's trailers only for the names its Trailer field announced, and the others are discarded before the handler runs
both reset the stream; the code, or the number of resets (a second HEADERS or DATA on a stream, Go's own body reader's error), differs

column1: # the reference reads the same bytes differently cut

column5: nghttp2 counts the pieces a header block arrives in as CONTINUATION frames (CVE-2024-28182 hardening), so a header block of two or more frames fed a byte at a time ends the connection and fed whole does not; DATA and field blocks cut at other places are read the same
h2 checks a chunk against the state the whole chunk leaves (a bad preface raises on every byte; a GOAWAY and what follows in one chunk is read in one), so the answer depends on the cut
Go's handler and its reader run concurrently: whether a request had been recorded, or its body read, when a later frame arrived depends on the timing of the cut
nghttp2 requires a block to open with a dynamic table size update after the decoder's maximum was set below 4096 (RFC 7541 section 4.2); this decoder, handed a table already of that size, does not

a dynamic table size update in the middle of a block (an inserted or changed octet of the form 001xxxxx) is a COMPRESSION_ERROR (RFC 7541 section 4.2: only at the start of a block); Go's decoder applies it wherever it comes
